115:         if not stuff:
116:             # Empty range: never match.
117:             return '(?!)', i
118:         elif stuff == '!':
119:             # Negated empty range: match any character.
120:             return dot, i
121:         else:
122:             if stuff[0] == '!':
123:                 stuff = '^' + stuff[1:]
124:             elif stuff[0] in ('^', '['):
125:                 stuff = '\\' + stuff
126:             return f'[{stuff}]', i
127: 
128: 
129: def _translate(pat):
130:     STAR = object()
131:     res = []
132:     add = res.append
133:     i, n = 0, len(pat)
134:     while i < n:
135:         c = pat[i]
136:         i = i+1
137:         if c == '*':
138:             # compress consecutive `*` into one
139:             while i < n and pat[i] == '*':
140:                 i = i+1
141:             add(STAR)
142:         elif c == '?':
143:             add('.')
144:         elif c == '[':
145:             res_str, i = _parse_bracket(pat, i, n, '.')
146:             add(res_str)
147:         else:
148:             add(re.escape(c))
149:     assert i == n
150: 
151:     # Deal with STARs.
152:     inp = res
153:     res = []
154:     add = res.append
155:     i, n = 0, len(inp)
156:     # Fixed pieces at the start?
157:     while i < n and inp[i] is not STAR:
158:         add(inp[i])
159:         i += 1
160:     # Now deal with STAR fixed STAR fixed ...
161:     # For an interior `STAR fixed` pairing, we want to do a minimal
162:     # .*? match followed by `fixed`, with no possibility of backtracking.
163:     # Atomic groups ("(?>...)") allow us to spell that directly.
164:     # Note: people rely on the undocumented ability to join multiple
165:     # translate() results together via "|" to build large regexps matching
166:     # "one of many" shell patterns.
167:     while i < n:
168:         assert inp[i] is STAR
169:         i += 1
170:         if i == n:
171:             add(".*")
172:             break
173:         assert inp[i] is not STAR
174:         fixed = []
175:         while i < n and inp[i] is not STAR:
176:             fixed.append(inp[i])
177:             i += 1
178:         fixed = "".join(fixed)
179:         if i == n:
180:             add(".*")
181:             add(fixed)
182:         else:
183:             add(f"(?>.*?{fixed})")
184:     assert i == n
185:     res = "".join(res)
186:     return fr'(?s:{res})\Z'
187:

189: def _translate_full(pat, sep):
190:     SEP = re.escape(sep)
191:     DOT = f'[^{SEP}]'
192:     res = []
193:     add = res.append
194:     i, n = 0, len(pat)
195:     while i < n:
196:         c = pat[i]
197:         i = i+1
198:         if c == '*':
199:             # compress consecutive `*` into one
200:             h = i-1
201:             while i < n and pat[i] == '*':
202:                 i = i+1
203:             star_count = i-h
204:             is_segment = (h == 0 or pat[h-1] == sep) and (i == n or pat[i] == sep)
205:             if star_count == 1:
206:                 if is_segment:
207:                     add(f'{DOT}+')
208:                 else:
209:                     add(f'{DOT}*')
210:             elif star_count == 2 and is_segment:
211:                 if i == n:
212:                     add('.*')
213:                 else:
214:                     add(f'(.*{SEP})?')
215:                     i = i+1
216:             else:
217:                 raise ValueError("Invalid pattern: '**' can only be an entire path component")
218:         elif c == '?':
219:             add(DOT)
220:         elif c == '[':
221:             res_str, i = _parse_bracket(pat, i, n, DOT)
222:             add(res_str)
223:         else:
224:             add(re.escape(c))
225:     assert i == n
226:     res = "".join(res)
227:     return fr'(?s:{res})\Z'
228:

230: def translate(pat, sep=None):
231:     """Translate a shell PATTERN to a regular expression.
232: 
233:     A path separator character may be supplied to the *sep* argument. If
234:     given, '*' and '?' wildcards will not match separators; '*' wildcards in
235:     standalone pattern segments match precisely one path segment; and  '**'
236:     wildcards in standalone segments match any number of path segments.
237: 
238:     There is no way to quote meta-characters.
239:     """
240:     if sep is None:
241:         return _translate(pat)
242:     else:
243:         return _translate_full(pat, sep)
